Subject: MedLumen Private/VPC deployment - post-call summary & next steps

Hi Daniel & Priya,

Thanks again for the productive call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Recap:
- Scope: MedLumen is evaluating a Private/VPC-hosted deployment (customer VPC with Redwood private control plane).
- Compliance drivers: HIPAA must be satisfied; GDPR noted for EU data subsets (you indicated patient metadata will remain in-region).
- Current posture: SOC 2 status discussed (you mentioned an ongoing program; see Q below).
- Network options: preference for network isolation; air-gapped option flagged as high-cost but potentially required for one pilot site.

Action items / asks for MedLumen (can you confirm the bullets below?):
1) SOC 2 status and expected Type II date (we heard Q1 2029 on the call — please confirm).
2) Any existing vendor questionnaire you can share or, alternatively, access details so we can send our draft.
3) High-level network diagram or sketch showing DMZ, VPC peering, bastion/Jumphosts and where the Redwood nodes would live (public internet? private endpoints?). Attach if possible.
4) Clarify whether MI/PHI will traverse public internet or must be contained entirely within a private network path.

My next steps from Redwood:
- I will loop in our security lead (Ben) and solutions engineer (Soojin) to start a focused vendor questionnaire and sketch our deployment options (VPC peering, private endpoints, and an air-gapped variant).
- We will prepare a short evidence list for SOC 2 / HIPAA readiness (what we typically ask for: network diagrams, data flow, retention requirements, KMS & key custody plan).

Please reply with the SOC 2 timing and whether you can share that network sketch. If you'd prefer, we can share a vendor questionnaire draft for you to redline; happy to send that this afternoon.

Thanks,

Jordan,

Thanks for the clear summary — exactly what we needed. A few quick points from our side: 

1) SOC 2 status: In progress. We completed our readiness gap assessment and engaged an external auditor. We expect Type II in-scope testing to complete by 2029-01-15 (Q1 2029). I will flag if anything moves earlier.

2) Network sketch: attaching a very high-level diagram (redacted) that shows our typical VPC layout for vendor integrations. This is intentionally high-level until legal greenlights a full diagram share.

3) Data flow: PHI will be contained within our VPC; we do not expect PHI to traverse the public internet. For some ancillary event logging (non-PHI), we may allow secure egress to third-party monitoring endpoints.

4) Vendor questionnaire: we do not have a standard vendor SQ beyond a short vendor intake form. Please send your questionnaire draft and we will route to security for redlines.

We appreciate Redwood outlining the air-gapped option — that is a possibility for our pilot in Phoenix if the vendor cannot meet our controlled network requirement.

Regards,

Thanks for the ping — reviewed Daniel's sketch and notes. I put together a short vendor SQ draft and a security checklist for an air-gapped engagement. High-level notes below and attached: redwood_vendor_questionnaire_draft.docx, security_checklist_airgap_v1.pdf.

High-level takeaways: 
- SOC 2: their timeline (2029-01-15) is acceptable for an initial pilot if contractual controls include interim attestations and an evidence-sharing cadence. Request auditor contact when available.
- Network isolation: the sketch is helpful. To proceed we need a concrete list of required inbound/outbound ports and target CIDRs. Also request expected NAT/Gateway behavior and whether they allow private endpoints backed by VPC peering or require a transit gateway.
- KMS: if they must retain key custody, we need to validate KMS provider and whether customer-managed keys can be provided to the Redwood Private runtime (we support BYOK; we will need KMS endpoint, key ARN and an administrative contact).
- Air-gapped option: feasible but requires local ops (container repo sync, patch windows, physical console access). Cost & timeline estimate: +6-10 weeks for provisioning and validation; ops runbook required.
- Evidence ask list (minimal): network diagram (full), SOC 2 readiness report, EULA/BAA request, encryption-at-rest/in-transit statements, admin access policy, and list of third-party sub-processors.

Next actions:
1) Jordan — send the vendor questionnaire to Daniel & Priya and propose Tue/Wed next week (I'll be available Tue afternoon PT).
2) Daniel/Priya — please share the detailed network diagram and the list of allowed CIDRs/ports; if you can't attach full diagrams, a redacted diagram plus a Contact in security who can receive full evidence will work.
3) Marissa/Soojin — start an internal cadence for an evidence review and map the ask list to our SOC 2 control evidence.

Attachments: redwood_vendor_questionnaire_draft.docx, security_checklist_airgap_v1.pdf
